correctness.rationale: Writing \(t=(C_1+C_2)/2\) and \(u=(C_1-C_2)/(C_1+C_2)\) gives metric eigenvalues \(t(1\pm r)\), where \(r=\sqrt{s^2+(1-s^2)u^2}\ge s\), with equality exactly at \(C_1=C_2\). For fixed \(r\), strict convexity for \(1<p<\infty\) gives the stated unique \(t_p(r)\), and substitution gives \(m_p(r)=2r/((1+r)^q+(1-r)^q)^{1/q}\). Its logarithmic derivative reduces to a strictly positive numerator, so the global optimum is uniquely at \(r=s\). The piecewise-linear \(p=1\) case and equioscillation \(p=\infty\) case similarly have unique fixed-\(r\) optima and increasing minima. The \(s=0\) boundary is included and still yields the unique identity metric. Independent numerical rechecks reproduced the formulas on representative \(s,p\) values.

value.rationale: The theorem closes an explicit family of alternative metric-selection problems raised by the motivating paper and reveals a structural invariant—the selected positive ray is independent of Schatten index—even though the normalization changes. final_claim: For every two-dimensional quasi-self-adjoint operator with simple real spectrum, every Schatten-\(p\) distance from the identity, \(1\le p\le\infty\), uniquely minimizes over the full positive metric family on the same ray \(C_1=C_2\), with the explicit coefficients and minimum distances stated in the record.
limitations: Distance is measured from the identity in Schatten norms; higher-dimensional, weighted, or differently normalized objectives are not covered.
